entries.title: Internet Archive copy of Newman, Glamorgan (1995): the catalogue description is a children's story blurb
entries.holder: Internet Archive (item metadata and its MARC, Dublin Core and meta files)
entries.reference: Internet Archive identifier glamorganmidglam0000newm; OCLC 33858574; ISBN 0140710566
entries.category: Catalogue description does not match the item
entries.said: The catalogue description of the Internet Archive copy: “A very hairy but not-too-scary monster story. One dark, stormy night, Owl, Mouse and Rabbit are afraid. Could it be the Monster of the Woods knocking at the door?”
entries.found: The item is John Newman’s Glamorgan (The Buildings of Wales, 1995), a 717-page architectural guide with entries for Llandough-juxta-Penarth (pp.378–379), Leckwith (pp.370–371) and Cogan.
entries.why: The summary note belongs to a children’s picture book. Searched by its description, the guide would not be found.

entries.title: Historic England · reply of 2026-10-21
entries.said: Historic England, 21 October 2026: “we do not hold any information that falls within the scope of your request.”
entries.found: Historic England, 27 October 2026: a letter of transfer to RCAHMW dated 12 January 2018.
entries.why: The first reply itself recorded the 12 January 2018 transfer; the covering letter followed six days after a challenge.

entries.title: Amgueddfa Cymru – Museum Wales · reply of 2026-08-25
entries.said: Amgueddfa Cymru – Museum Wales, 25 August 2026: “Amgueddfa Cymru does not hold the requested information.”
entries.found: Museum Wales, 22 September 2026: records of archaeological discoveries recorded at Great House Farm and Church Farm, Llandough, identified in the searches for the first request.
entries.why: The records were found in the first search and set aside as outside its scope; they were released four weeks later on a fresh request.

entries.title: Glamorgan Archives DBDT/79/1: catalogue description corrected after the original was examined (14 September 2026)
entries.said: Catalogue entry: “Lease (counterpart) of land and premises situate in Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff, from the Marquess of Bute to Mr John Williams, May 1877.”
entries.found: Examined at our request, the original is a counterpart lease of 2 May 1877 from the Trustees of the Will of the late Marquess of Bute to Mr John Williams of Newport. Glamorgan Archives: “The catalogue description for DBDT/79/1 had a few small errors which have now been corrected.”
entries.why: A physical check of the original, asked for on 26 August 2026, found the catalogue wording wrong. The deed concerns Pembroke Terrace, Cardiff; the archive found no mention of Llandough in it.

entries.title: Vale of Glamorgan Council · reply of 2026-06-02
entries.said: Vale of Glamorgan Council, 2 June 2026: “the Vale of Glamorgan Council does not hold records relating to this historic legal matter.”
entries.found: Vale of Glamorgan Council, 11 September 2026: “further historical documentation has been found.” Not yet disclosed.
entries.why: Found once service areas were asked again; the council is still sifting it.

entries.title: Welsh Government / Cadw · reply of 2026-02-25
entries.said: Cadw, 25 February 2026: “much of the content in your correspondence falls outside the scope of Cadw’s work.”
entries.found: Cadw, 21 May 2026: its electronic records held the 1988 listing assessment of Great House Farm and Barn, and two photographs dated 29 July 1988.
entries.why: The records were in Cadw’s own system; they came out once a request named the property and the 1988 survey.
